title: Opus 5.5 helped me building all of this and me and my friends are having a blast in the current playtest!
author: Jealous_Fan4986
selftext:
7 days ago I started a game about grandparents racing wheelchairs after the pub. Last night we had our first playtest and I can't stop laughing

I started the project 7 days ago. I didn't want to use AI at all, but one of my friends convinced me to try "getting a little bit of help", and that little bit of help BOOSTED the entire project.

I was NEVER expecting to have such a fun and entertaining playtest!

The game is called AfterPub. It's a chaotic party game where pensioners leave the pub and settle things by racing on wheelchairs.

It's still very early and rough around the edges, so I'd love some honest feedback:

\- What would make you want to play a game like this with your friends?

\- Which mode sounds the most fun to you?

If you want to follow along, you can find the project on steam in few days.  
for now you can find us on discord: [https://discord.gg/bpTWxxGwj8](https://discord.gg/bpTWxxGwj8)



Thanks for reading, and may your grandma never drift past you on the last corner 👵💨

replies.author: Jealous_Fan4986
replies.body:
And trust me I was slow, between work and real life stuff this was a really slow process.

I used Godot and Opus 5.5.

No single prompt, given proper feedback and I designed the UI my self, indeed the shop is garbage, so most definitely will be reworked! I used mixamo for some of the animations, rest is procedurally generated as the high speed movements would break the animations.

Characters are generated with Tripo (Only few with SmartMesh) and the Banners are Astra in light effort.

Ideas,balance, minigames, steamworks comes from me as that's literally what I do for work! I asked Claude to still optimize code and correct me if there was something wrong.

Ask anything else if you need! I'll happily answer

(also the name afterpub, but many of the games are "in the pub" is confusing? or do you mean games you can play with your mates after you got kicked out of the pub because you talked too much on how AI is going to change the world too loudly)

replies.author: Jealous_Fan4986
replies.body:
Thanks for the honest feedback, I really appreciate it! I get why it can look confusing, but there's a reason there are so many games.

The main mode is the race itself, which is what happens after the grandpas and grannies get kicked out of the pub (hence the name). Racing earns you rank points (not a real competitive mode) and unlocks cosmetics that are exclusive to that mode.

The pub games (that's why they're called pub games) are where you earn coins. Coins buy paint for your wheelchair, banners, titles, victory celebrations and other fancy stuff, so you can literally show off how much time you've spent in the game. Every cosmetic is earned by playing, and there are no microtransactions at all.

Betting is in every mode. Spectators and people in the same party can bet on you or against you winning the round, game or prize, so nobody gets left out, even if they joined the lobby late or just want to watch :)

The trailer not focusing only on the races is intentional. I didn't want to make a racing game, but more of a "hey, let's just casually play something together" game. You hop in with your friends, race a few rounds, play some poker or beer pong in between, and bet on each other the whole time.

That said, you're right that some of the pub games look less polished than the races right now. That's good feedback and I'm working on bringing them up to the same level. Also the AI line made me laugh, that's probably exactly how half of them got kicked out lol

replies.author: 3dutchie3dprinting
replies.body:
I think I get it... but if the main aim is racing and that takes place outside, the rest is basically put "micro games for cosmetics used in the race" it's odd that the game title is aimed at the "micro" part of the game instead of the main part right?

"Geriatric racer" (as an example) for the game makes sense and then anything in the pub will be the micro games (and can then even just be less polished since they're nice to have activities)

  
I'm not here to question your game btw, just trying to be a voice of reason you're 100% more than welcome to ignore ;-)

replies.author: Jealous_Fan4986
replies.body:
Not at all, I appreciate it! This is exactly the kind of feedback I need this early, so please keep it coming!!

The name actually comes from the whole night rather than one mode. AfterPub is the moment the pub closes and everyone spills out onto the street: the race home is the main event, but the drinks, the bets and the stupid games with your mates are all part of that same night out. That's the vibe I'm going for, a casual "night out with the grandpas" party game, not a pure racer.

That's also why I avoided something like "Geriatric Racer". It's a great name for a racing game, but it would set the expectation that racing is all there is, and then people would feel the same confusion the other way round when they find poker and beer pong in there.

You do have a point that the pub games shouldn't feel like they're competing with the races for attention, though. The races will stay the heart of the game, and I'll make sure the next update for the store page and trailer show that more clearly, so the pub games come across as the fun extras around it.

Thanks again for taking the time, it genuinely helps, we grow trough feedbacks and criticism
